neighbours.label: first-person singular narrator (I / me / my) in narrative and dialogue
fire: The lights went out at midnight, and then I heard footsteps on the stairs.
"You're late again," the coach told me as soon as I walked into the gym.
Later that summer my uncle took us fishing on the lake behind his cabin.
When the train finally stopped, Maria and I grabbed our bags and ran.
The old sailor looked at me for a long moment before he answered.
After the storm passed, I climbed onto the roof to check the damage.
"Did you lock the door?" Sam asked me as we pulled out of the driveway.
That evening my grandmother told stories about the war until dawn.
quiet: The lights went out at midnight, and then she heard footsteps on the stairs.
"You're late again," the coach told him as soon as he walked into the gym.
Later that summer their uncle took them fishing on the lake behind his cabin.
When the train finally stopped, Maria and Tom grabbed their bags and ran.
The old sailor looked at the boy for a long moment before he answered.
After the storm passed, the farmer climbed onto the roof to check the damage.
"Did you lock the door?" Sam asked her as they pulled out of the driveway.
That evening their grandmother told stories about the war until dawn.
